newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi dinar sinks despite oil euphoria.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi dinar sinks despite oil euphoria.

text.p: Iraq's dinar currency sank on Thursday despite euphoria over the resumption of partial Iraqi oil exports to world markets.
Traders said the dinar plummeted to 1,100 to the U.S. dollar from around 800 early in December.
They said uncertainty about the fate of dinars which the government printed to balance budget deficts in the six years of crippling U.N. trade sanctions was behind the dinar's sudden slump.
The governor of the central bank, Isam Hweish, issued a statement on Wednesday denying rumours that the government had plans to change the currency.
The ruling Revolutionary Command Council, the highest executive body in Iraq, also issued a new decree toughening penalties against hard cash smugglers.

Traders said Iraqis with excessive cash started feverish buying of the dollar when its value nosedived on the news of Iraq's agreeing to U.N. demands on partial oil exports late last month. The dollar temporarily fell to around 600 dinars from 1,650 on the news.
Prices of essential commodities also soared. A kilo of sugar jumped to 625 dinars from 400 and a tray of 30 eggs skyrocketed to 2,600 from 1,250.
The oil deal with the U.N. allows sales of $2 billion worth of oil over six months to enable Iraq buy badly needed food and medicine for its sanctions-hit population.

On Wednesday the trade ministry said the deal would enable it to boost food rations it distributes to millions of Iraqis at giveaway prices. The meagre rations are now hardly enough to meet one-third of a person's monthly needs for essential items.
